questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Wanted to go to the UK, and was the only place that had the Erasmus grant. Had been to England but not Scotland

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There's an app called edinburgh uni events with events for the first week by students. Otherwise I got the information in mail. there was a lot of paperwork but that is to be expected

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: You get a student councilor that you can write to or meet with

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Me and 5 other students found housing in february already, very difficult to find housing

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: check your contracts

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Confirmation of attendance both for the uni and for Erasmus so was a bit confusing that you had to do it twice, but one was for uni and another for your visa

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Student advisor and various other services offered by the uni. Everything from mental health to housing contracts

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Had friends that had difficulty since the original classes they choose were overlapping and it took a long time to find another course since the courses on sociology get full very quick. I however was lucky and had a fairly easy time with registering

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont be afraid to message them, and find and use the other students going so you can help eachother

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I am a bit unsure but they were bachelor and at least one of them had quite a few students on their first semester so was an entry course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mix of lectures and dialogue. Quite similar to UCPH. Certain expectations to participate in dialogue, but the questions were never difficult and more about discussion

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Understanding Public Policy
Religion and Society
Popular music, Technology and Society

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Was the last time Popular music was available sadly

Michael is a great and funny teacher in religion and society, highly recommend!

Understanding Public Policy could be a bit hit or miss depending on the theory and lecturer, but learned a lot of interesting theories and as someone that have missed a focus on politics as a sociology student I was very happy with the course. Did however feel that the seminars (holdundervisning) was a waste of time but the course itself was good.

questions.question: Insurance DKK *
Housing DKK per month *
Books DKK per month *
Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *
Other fees DKK per month *
What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Heating and electricity were quite expensive. There were five of us living there and we paid 350kr per month per person, but we also lived in a big cold apartment. They call it the cost of living crisis over here!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Monthly bus pass is the same as dk and fairly necessary
Beer is a bit cheaper but not much
Cigarettes cost 120kr if you're into that! lots of cheap vapes in return

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Soooo many societies with events all the time

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Just check out the different societies and join one you find enjoyable

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Erasmus student network has different trips. Went to Loch Ness as a day trip and it was good 

I would however recommend planning your own trips. Did one with friends to Inverness/Isle of Skye and it was the best part of the semester!

Go on walks around Edinburgh 

Pubquizzes!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Nice that everyone speak english. Scotland is very multicultural and inclusive with nice people. Had a lot of danish friends so also cheated a bit in that sense

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to events, join a society, go out to events at bars

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None that i can think of

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Pubs!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Look at events/societies and go to stuff 

Go to the highlands one way or another, its special!

Dont stress too much with school, As a sociology students it wasn't that diffucult compared to CPH, but may be different for other subjects

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you go with private renting, then the deposit has to go though a third party controlled by the council, look it up

Download the app previously mentioned and follow the different societies on instagram/facebook

Find the erasmus student network instagram and join the whatsapp-group (and turn off notifications)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The culture, nature, pubs, food, friends

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Busses were unpredictable and drove pretty crazy. Could take between 20 and 50 minitues to go to uni from Inverleith where i stayed. Missed being able to bike

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
